subject: Post-demo: feature econ deep-dive, token bands & CAC payback
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@medsync.health>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@carehub.io>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — quick follow up on volumes + pricing bands

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Tom and I found the latency and routing controls compelling for our triage workflows. A couple quick asks from our side so we can pull procurement and product finance into the loop: 

- Expected monthly token range we discussed was rough — can you confirm the unit bands we should model (low/med/high)?
- We need a target $/1M tokens figure to compare against current vendor spend.
- Can you provide a simple "$/feature" example for our primary triage action (single-turn summary + classification)?

High-level context: we expect ~10k active end users initially, ~2–4 feature calls per user/day, and average prompt+response length ~600 tokens. Budgeting team wants a 12–18 month CAC payback target and >40% gross margin on features.

If you send a short recap (numbers + next steps) we'll loop in procurement.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Product
MedSync Health
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@medsync.health>, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@carehub.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick follow up on volumes + pricing bands

Elena / Tom — thanks for the time. Recap and numbers below (quick, actionable):

1) Token bands (modeling guidance) — based on your call guidance and our experience across similar triage products: 
   - Low: 1M tokens / month  (pilot phase)
   - Mid: 5M tokens / month (initial scale / month 3–6)
   - High: 20M tokens / month (full rollout + feature expansion)

2) Typical request sizing assumption we used: 
   - Prompt + response = 600 tokens (average)
   - Feature calls/user/day = 3 (conservative)
   - Active users = 10k -> daily tokens ~ 18M -> monthly ~ 540M (this is upper-bound if all users active every day).
   - For budgeting I recommend modeling on per-feature active cohort (10–30% of MAU) — leads to our token bands above.

3) Target $/1M tokens (pricing hypotheses):
   - Pilot band (1M): $420 / 1M tokens (includes hosted SLA + observability)
   - Mid band (5M): $210 / 1M tokens (committed discount applied)
   - High band (20M): $95 / 1M tokens (dedicated capacity/quantization recommendations)

   Notes: these are list examples; final pricing depends on model family, quantization, and prefix caching opportunities. We'll run a workload profile to confirm realistic per-token cost.

4) $/feature worked example (single-turn summary + classification):
   - Avg tokens per call: 600
   - Tokens per feature call => 0.0006 * 1M = 600 tokens => 0.6k tokens (i.e. 0.6k/1M fraction).
   - At $210 / 1M tokens -> cost per call = $210 * (600 / 1,000,000) = $0.126 per feature call.
   - At $95 / 1M tokens -> cost per call = $0.057 per feature call.

5) Unit economics sketch (simple):
   - Assume feature monetization = $0.40 revenue per call (packaged into subscription or usage credits).
   - At $0.126 cost -> gross margin per call = 68%. At $0.057 cost -> margin = 86%.
   - CAC payback: if new user contributes 9 feature calls in first 30 days, revenue/month per new user = 9 * $0.40 = $3.6. To hit 12-month payback on CAC, allowable CAC = 12 * $3.6 = $43.2 per new user. Adjust with churn and expansion.

6) Immediate asks / next steps: 
   - I: Redwood to send an economic model (attached) with slots to plug your MAU/activation/feature-frequency. (att: econ-sample-model.xlsx)
   - II: If procurement wants a PO/procurement path, we'll draft an MAP; attach mutual-action-plan.docx for review.
   - III: Proposed follow-up: 30-minute finance deep-dive on Fri 4/23 at 10am PT — align on bands and commitment sizing.

Attachments: econ-sample-model.xlsx (simple tab with token bands + per-feature calc), mutual-action-plan.docx, demo recording link.

Cc'ing Marissa and Ben for pricing & commercial guidance. Marissa — any adjustments on the suggested $/1M bands or packaging? Ben — can you confirm SLA/commit thresholds for dedicated capacity?

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Elena Morales <elena@medsync.health>, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@carehub.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: feature econ deep-dive, token bands & CAC payback

Thanks Karthik — quick commercial notes from pricing: 

- Bands look directionally right. I'd tweak the pilot list price to $350 / 1M to keep runway for initial discounting.
- For mid band (5M) we can offer a 3-month introductory at $180 / 1M then step to $210. That helps procurement justify short-term savings.
- For high band (20M) confirm dedicated capacity SKU: requires 3-month commit and initial validation workload; once validated, we can move to $85 / 1M. Ben, confirm the SLA/commit we need to put in the MAP.

Commercial packaging suggestion (simple):
- Pilot: 1M tokens/month, 3-month minimum, support included, monthly usage billing.
- Growth: 5M tokens/month, quarterly invoicing, 10% discount on overage if committed.
- Scale: Dedicated capacity quote with fixed monthly EDP-style pricing and a performance SLA.

Elena — I'll join the Fri 4/23 call and bring a one-page quote table. Also attaching a streamlined MAP template for procurement review (see mutual-action-plan.docx).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: feature econ deep-dive, token bands & CAC payback

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few clarifying items before we pull procurement in: 

1) Can you add a quick row in the model for a conservative adoption scenario: 10% of MAU using the feature daily (instead of the cohort approach)? That will help reconcile our internal forecast.
2) For CAC math — our finance team treats CAC against new-paid accounts (not MAU). I'll share a compact cohort projection ahead of the call; could you surface the per-new-account payback at the $180 and $95 bands?
3) Security question: for the dedicated SKU, does Redwood offer customer-managed KMS? We need this for our security checklist.

If you can confirm those three items and forward an updated one-page quote, we'll schedule procurement and legal to join the Fri slot if that still works.

Thanks — Elena
